item.title: Anthony Rizzo shares urgent MLB lockout warning amid salary cap dilemma
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Eric Canha-Imagn Images Anthony Rizzo shares urgent MLB lockout warning amid salary cap dilemma appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . MLB unfortunately seems to be headed for a lockout. Players and owners are on completely different sides of the salary cap debate . There are other topics that will impact the new collective bargaining agreement discussions, but the salary cap is the most pressing issue at the moment. The MLBPA as well as MLB will continue to look for solutions , but a lockout will occur if a new deal isn’t reached by early December. Former MLB star Anthony Rizzo shared his thoughts on the topic during a recent segment of Ross and Rizzo Unfiltered. “Look, no one wants to lose baseball,” Rizzo said. “… Baseball is in a great spot, it’s very competitive. But with this lockout, with the owners digging down and saying they’re going salary cap, I need fans to understand, forever baseball hasn’t had a salary cap. There’s so much that needs to happen in this CBA negotiation that this could drag out unfortunately longer than expected.” Baseball would be dealt a brutal blow if games end up being missed due to the lockout. The game is indeed in a “great spot” right now as Rizzo mentioned. If the situation does end up dragging out “longer than expected” like Rizzo said, baseball will be in an especially challenging position. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) MLB has worked hard to bounce back after it seemed as if the sport’s popularity was trending in the wrong direction not too long ago. The rule changes to the game such as the pitch clock and ABS challenge system have seemingly led to an increase in fan interest in the sport once again. So, what may it take for the owners and players to put their differences aside and find a solution? Rizzo, who, again, was a star at the MLB level, admitted money could be the breaking point. “But until there’s an actual deadline, until owners start losing money — which is not going to be for a long time into the lockout — or players start feeling it on their paychecks, things aren’t going to start moving unfortunately.” Rizzo surely hopes he’s wrong about things potentially taking longer than anticipated to resolve, but his take should not be overlooked. item.description: Trevor Ruszkowski-Imagn Images Braden Smith just showed the NBA what happens when a team runs out of stars. The rookie from Purdue scored 19 points and handed out 10 assists in a game where the Indiana Pacers started six players because everyone else was hurt or resting. The Hawks managed to escape with a 108-104 win on Monday night, but they nearly got upset by a squad that was missing its entire starting lineup. This loss for Atlanta feels like a lucky escape rather than a dominant performance, and the numbers tell the whole story. A Salary Gap That Makes No Sense The financial disparity in this game was absurd. According to Peachtree Hoops , bench players totaled roughly $193 million in salary, whereas active roster members earned approximately $15 million. That is a difference of nearly $200 million between the bench and the active roster. The Pacers were forced to play three players on two-way contracts just to get a game in. Tyrese Haliburton and TJ McConnell were among the names missing, leaving Smith as the only pure point guard available. He stepped up and ran the offense like a veteran, proving the team has depth but lacks the payroll flexibility to keep everyone healthy. Atlanta had their own issues to deal with. Jalen Johnson was sidelined with an ankle tweak, and Jock Landale also missed out. Even with these absences, the Hawks held on, but it was closer than it should have been. Nickeil Alexander-Walker led the way with 34 points and hit nine three-pointers to tie his career best. Hawks head coach Quin Snyder admitted the win was tough to earn. “It’s a really good win,” said Snyder postgame, acknowledging the team was not at their best inside the rim. Smith Earns More Minutes Immediately Braden Smith did not just survive his first start; he dominated it. He spent 42 minutes on the floor and shot 8 of 13 from the field. Before this game, he had played only 18 total NBA minutes and scored a single point. He found out at walk-through that he would start, yet he attacked the basket with confidence. He has had to get used to not touching the ball every possession. “I’m such a rhythm guy,” Embiid said. “And over the years, obviously, I’ve had a lot of opportunities to just touch the ball almost every other possession.” This adjustment has been part of the team’s success, as the starting lineup combined for 102 points in the last win. item.description: Spurs face three big decisions with January looming Tottenham Academy Loans in Focus as Luca Gunter Eyes January Move Tottenham’s season is beginning to gather a little rhythm under Roberto De Zerbi and, in the background, another important story is developing, one that often tells you just as much about a club’s health as events on a Saturday afternoon. According to Standard , young goalkeeper Luca Gunter is set to assess his loan options in January after being recalled from Boreham Wood last month. It is a small detail on the surface, but it speaks to a wider truth about how modern clubs try to bridge the gap between academy promise and senior football reality. Gunter had embedded himself quickly at Boreham Wood, becoming first choice and playing a prominent role in a side that has made an unbeaten start in the National League. Those are not throwaway appearances, they are the kind of matches that begin to harden a young player and teach him the weight of responsibility. Luca Gunter Recall Creates Fresh Tottenham Decision The recall came after an injury to third-choice goalkeeper Brandon Austin, with Gunter returning to train around the first team at Spurs. The expectation is that he will remain in that environment for now before looking to head back out on loan when the January window opens. That feels sensible. A goalkeeper’s development can stall in a hurry if minutes disappear, and while exposure to senior training at Tottenham has obvious value, competitive football remains the currency that matters most. Tottenham Academy Prospects Facing January Choices Gunter is not the only one weighing his next step. Tyrese Hall is expected to attract both loan and permanent interest, while Under-21s captain James Rowswell could also seek a move after failing to secure one in the summer. These are the sorts of decisions that can shape a career long before the wider public has fully noticed a player’s name. Photo IMAGO There are encouraging signs, too. De Zerbi has shown a growing willingness to involve academy players as results have improved, and Luca Williams-Barnett was handed his Premier League debut against Crystal Palace. Others, including Tye Hall and Callum Olusesi, have also been brought closer to the senior set-up. Roberto De Zerbi Pathway Offers Spurs Encouragement For Tottenham, this is the balancing act. Gunter’s next move may look modest from afar, yet these are often the decisions that help decide whether an academy produces hopefuls or genuine first-team players. The Arizona Fall League is a great opportunity for prospects to either prove themselves or make up for lost time. Nats prospect Jarlin Susana falls into both of those categories. item.description: Djokovic's 24 Grand Slam singles titles are a men's record but have him tied with Margaret Court overall [Getty Images] Novak Djokovic is out of the race to qualify for the ATP Finals in Turin after a second-round defeat by qualifier Rinky Hijikata at the Paris Masters. It means Djokovic, 39, has failed to qualify for the event for only the second time in the past 20 seasons when fit. The Serb likely needed to reach the semi-finals in Paris to qualify, although the draw had appeared to open up for him after two of his rivals for a place fell earlier in the day. Despite a good start, Djokovic was unable to repel Australian world number 83 Hijikata in a 2-6 6-3 6-3 defeat. As Hijikata lifted his level at the end of the second set and throughout the decider, Djokovic, who appeared laboured and to be struggling physically, produced a series of errors, bringing an end to his season. Zverev annoyed by reaction to becoming world number one Death threats for Briton Burrage on WTA Tour return Despite reaching the final of the Australian Open and the semi-finals of Wimbledon, Djokovic has not reached the quarter-final in any of this year's Masters 1000 events. He won the last of his 24 Grand Slam titles at the US Open in 2023. Qualifying for Turin would have given him a chance to win a record-extending eighth title at the season-ending championships. Instead, only Americans Taylor Fritz and Tommy Paul remain in contention to take the final two places currently held by Frances Tiafoe and Rafael Jodar. Djokovic had not failed to qualify when fit since 2017. Tiafoe's chances were taken out of his hands earlier on Wednesday when he fell to a 6-3 1-6 7-6 (11-9) defeat by Frenchman Quentin Halys. Australian Alex de Minaur then failed to take advantage as he lost 7-6 (7-2) 6-3 to Argentine Tomas Martin Etcheverry. A run in Paris could have secured De Minaur's qualification. Elsewhere, world number one Alexander Zverev and fourth seed Daniil Medvedev, both of whom have already qualified for Turin, were also beaten. item.title: Tom Brady Returns To Foxborough As Fox Broadcaster
item.description: Joe Nicholson-Imagn Images The moment fans have waited six years is finally here. Tom Brady returns to Foxborough on Sunday not as the man in the huddle, but as the voice in the booth. Erin Andrews is already stoking the fire for this massive homecoming. She posted the official hype video on her Instagram story with zero words, letting the moment speak for itself per Yahoo Sports . He told Colin Cowherd on Tuesday that the experience will be “certainly emotional.” The legend spent two decades walking every inch of that stadium, from the locker rooms to the meeting rooms. Before moving to Tampa in 2020, he guided the Patriots to six titles and nine Super Bowl appearances. Now he returns to call a game against the Green Bay Packers. It is a strange role for a man who once held the fate of the franchise in his hands. The View From The Booth Brady will sit alongside Kevin Burkhardt for the 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff. This marks his first time calling a Patriots game since joining Fox Sports in 2022. Andrews and Tom Rinaldi will handle the sideline work. The setup feels right for a team that just beat Miami 24-19. Brady admitted he is “very, very excited” to be there in front of a friendly home crowd. He noted that the Packers are a team he already covered this year and knows well. The matchup features two 5-3 teams. Fox made the game official early this week, releasing a preview that fans have been waiting for. A New Perspective on the Patriots What makes this return unique is Brady’s new take on the current squad. He praised the 2026 Patriots for starting slow and then going on a tear. He called quarterback Drake Maye an MVP candidate after the team faced the Seahawks in the Super Bowl last February. “I’m really talking about this awesome program that’s been built,” Brady said. According to him, the Patriots consistently manage to execute things correctly. He will be calling a game that includes his former team and must remain impartial. The bias test begins when he puts on the headset. Brady’s contract with Fox is a reported 10-year, $375 million deal. He must remain impartial while covering a team he once played for. CD Tenerife’s Spanish striker Jesus de Miguel died today as a result of a blow sustained during the match against Andorra from goalkeeper Jesus Owono, which caused him to go into cardiac arrest. (is associated with: «De Miguel funeral set for Thursday as Owono breaks silence») Europa Press Canarias/EUROPA PRESS/dpa Footballer Jesús de Miguel is set to be buried on Thursday, Spanish media reported, with his club CD Tenerife planning a memorial service at their stadium on Saturday. De Miguel died on Tuesday after suffering a cardiac arrest during a Spanish second-division match on Monday following a violent collision with Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono. The keeper, who was sent off for the foul near the halfway line, is being investigated by police. The burial will take place in Navahermosa, the family's home municipality in the province of Toledo, broadcaster Cadena SER reported on Wednesday. The family have thanked people for their condolences but, according to the club, have asked fans "to fully respect their privacy at this terrible time." The club will also pay their respects at a service at the Heliodoro Rodríguez López Stadium on the Canary Island on Saturday, with all fans invited. item.title: How landmark Everton compensation prevented Burnley record loss
item.description: Burnley were bought by ALK Capital in December 2020 using loans secured against the club's assets and other external debt [Getty Images] Six years ago, Burnley were considered one of the best-run clubs in the country. The Clarets were debt free, with £41.65m cash in the bank, and enjoying their fifth successive season of Premier League football. Now they sit in the Championship relegation zone, with concerns over debt and the way the Clarets were bought by ALK Capital using loans and the club's own money. Fans have been very concerned about what the future holds - although on Wednesday there was some rare positive news in the club's accounts. BBC Sport takes a closer look at what is going on at Turf Moor. How did ALK Capital buy the club? You may be familiar with the term "leverage buyout" after the Glazer family's purchase of Manchester United in 2005. It effectively means that a purchase is carried out using debt secured on the club's assets, its own bank balance and other loans, rather than the equity of the buyer. In Burnley's case, ALK Capital took out a £65m loan secured against the club's assets, such as Turf Moor , and used £37m from the club's own bank balance. On top of that, Velocity Capital, the holding company, owed Burnley £80.1m - money which was also used to buy the club. The original £65m loan was partially paid off, but then refinanced and extended to reach £105m in the 2024-25 accounts. Interest rates were as high as 12%. On top of that were factored debts, when a club mortgages off future transfer instalments for a one-off payment from the bank. Burnley owed £37m at an interest rate of 12.75%. In total, the football club's borrowings stood at £142.3m, the 10th-highest external debt in English football. Then came the 2025-26 accounts, published today, which painted a different picture. How owners finally paid off £77.7m used to buy Burnley Now, back to that leveraged buyout which has been attracting so much criticism from fans. Last season's accounts contained a big surprise. Remember Velocity Capital, the holding company that owed Burnley £80.1m for the purchase of the club? The accounts revealed £77.7m of that has now been paid to the Clarets. It cleared a large chunk of the debt used to buy the football club and helped to make the latest accounts look healthier. This was needed because, over the past six years, debts related to the leveraged buyout and associated interest payments had increased. Why Everton's £38.1m compensation was so vital for Burnley The £77.7m payment does not mean all Burnley's financial concerns or debts have been resolved. The club still reported a loss for 2025-26 of £9m, compared with £24m-£29m in the previous three seasons. That might seem positive. But this includes the Velocity Capital payment, money for being in the Premier League - and a landmark compensation payout. item.title: Bears Likely Hold Kyle Monangai Out For Sunday Night Game
item.description: Mike Dinovo-Imagn Images Don’t expect Kyle Monangai to line up against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers this Sunday. The injury timeline just does not work for a Week 9 return. Monangai has missed four straight games with a thumb injury and turf toe issues. The team kept him off the injured reserve list to save a spot, hoping he would be ready within a four-week window. That window has closed. The Chicago Tribune’s Brad Biggs wrote Tuesday that the team is unlikely to rush him back. The Practice Problem Monangai has not returned to practice yet. Biggs noted that rushing a player back after a month of inactivity is risky. “I’m skeptical they would have Monangai back for two practices — max — after missing a month and then add him to the mix Sunday night against the Buccaneers,” Biggs wrote Tuesday. Two days of practice is barely enough to shake off rust. The Bears need him healthy for the long haul, not just for one prime-time game. The smart play is to wait. A return on Nov. 22 against the New Orleans Saints at Soldier Field is what Biggs suggests targeting. Short Yardage Struggles The team has won three of their last four games without him, but the offense still feels the gap. Through eight weeks, the league’s No. 2 rushing offense belongs to Chicago. Roschon Johnson and veteran D’Andre Swift have stepped up well. Swift posted a season-low 2.6 yards per carry during the victory against Seattle. That number shows the team misses Monangai’s hard-charging style on short-yardage downs. Johnson is serviceable, but he lacks the same takeover ability. Twice during the first four games, Monangai hit 100 yards. The Bears need that specific skill set for the stretch run. Waiting for the Bye Head coach Ben Johnson has hinted that another back could see more time soon. The team signed Zavier Scott from the practice squad to the 53-man roster. Johnson said, “We’ve had him up for the last three weeks here, and it’s just been a matter of … that trust level.” Scott played strictly on special teams in Week 8. Johnson observed that if the team requires more bodies, “If that continues to be a thing, I think we’re going to need all three backs to play for us.” Keeping Monangai out until after the Week 10 bye makes the most sense. It gives him time to heal while the team relies on the current rotation. The bye week will provide the extra rest needed to get him fully ready for November.

item.title: Former Yankee pitcher explains retirement decision: ‘Nothing really materialized’
item.description: Chad Green, a reliable bullpen arm for the Yankees from 2016-22, has confirmed his retirement from MLB. “I officially just called it quits in April, early April,” Green said in an interview with Randy Olson of AreaSports. “I was still throwing and stuff once I got designated last year. I was still kind of working out and throwing and getting ready just in case an offer was worth it and something that I could leave and go do. But nothing really materialized… I really only called it quits in April.” The Toronto Blue Jays designated Green for assignment on July 29, 2025, after acquiring reliever Seranthony Dominguez. The Blue Jays then released Green in August 2025, effectively bringing his career to an end. Green was selected by the Detroit Tigers in the 11th round of the 2013 MLB draft out of Louisville. He was traded to the Yankees in December 2015 and made his major-league debut in 2016. With the Yankees in 2017, Green went 5-0 with a 1.83 ERA and 103 strikeouts over 69 innings. “When you’re going through a year like that, you don’t even realize what’s going on,” Green said. “New York was a place we’re not familiar with. Me and my wife had never been there before, so it’s like what do we do, where do we stay, how do we get to the ballpark, so things are happening so fast and you’re pitching well on top of it, a year like that goes by so fast. “Having success early on definitely helps you set yourself up way better down the line.” MORE BY ADAM ZAGORIA Former Yankees slugger wins U.S. House seat in Texas Nov. 4, 2026, 10:18 a.m. Brewers manager called Brian Cashman after controversial Yankees comments Nov. 4, 2026, 9:13 a.m. He had Tommy John surgery in 2022. “I didn’t finish my Yankee career the way I wanted it, had Tommy John surgery,” he said. “I knew that time was coming to an end, just how they operate, and they don’t sign guys who are hurt. item.title: Mauricio Pochettino doubles down on USMNT youth movement as Nations League stakes rise
item.description: Mauricio Pochettino expanded his U.S. player pool earlier this fall by inviting about a dozen young players for a series of friendlies. Most performed so well, they earned callbacks Wednesday — even with most veterans available for the first official matches since the World Cup and a youth-specific Olympic camp taking place at the same time. Cavan Sullivan, Julian Hall, Justin Ellis, Mathis Albert, Adri Mehmeti, Neil Pierre and Diego Kochen all parlayed their efforts in September-October into November invitations for the Nations League quarterfinals . Average age: 18.1. “We are playing now an official game [and] the priority always is for the first team,” Pochettino said Wednesday. “And because we all believe that if the players are involved with the first team, [there] is the possibility to keep growing and of course adding more experience — and good experience. It's easy.” The U.S. will begin workouts Monday at the national training center near Atlanta in preparation for the CONCACAF Nations League quarterfinals vs. Haiti. The first leg, or Haitian “home” game, is Nov. 14 in Miami, followed by the decider Nov. 17 in Cincinnati. Pochettino also invited three outsiders: Midfielder Santiago Castañeda, 21, and defender Reed Baker-Whiting, 21, will join their first senior camp and defender Bryan Reynolds, 25, will seek his first appearance for the U.S. since 2023. “Now it's a moment we need to add players to the roster to try to provide a good balance to the team,” Pochettino said of the 2030 World Cup cycle. “It's a great opportunity for different players now, and … to have the possibility to mix younger with experienced players.” Cavan Sullivan is among seven young USMNT prospects who earned another call-up after impressing during the team's four-game winning streak earlier this fall. Taylor Banner/USSF via Getty Images The young influx comes at the expense of seasoned players, such as Tim Weah, Brenden Aaronson, Matt Turner and Joe Scally. In addition, Yunus Musah was passed over after playing in the recent friendlies. The Indianapolis Colts are trading key pieces from their NFL roster this season to recoup some draft capital as they enter what could be a lengthy multi-year rebuild after firing Chris Ballard. item.title: Houston Astros Face Major Shake-Up After Wild Card Sweep
item.description: Thomas Shea-Imagn Images The Houston Astros won their division this year, but the victory feels hollow. A historic upset saw the White Sox eliminate them in the opening round. This loss proves that winning the West is not enough when the team cannot beat a lower-seeded opponent. Owner Jim Crane decided that the current path leads nowhere. He fired general manager Dana Brown in August and will not keep manager Joe Espada for next year. A New Leader Takes the Helm Randy Flores has been named the new general manager. He spent years as an assistant general manager and scouting director for the St. Louis Cardinals. Per MLB Trade Rumors , Flores will have a say in hiring the new bench boss for 2027. The organization needs a fresh voice to fix a roster that looks uneven. Although the squad remains competitive, its top talents are aging or approaching free agency. This leadership change signals a shift in how the club approaches the game. Money Tied Up in Aging Stars The financial picture for the Astros is tight and complicated. They have committed $168.35 million just for the 2027 season alone. Total future commitments reach $261.35 million, according to MLB Trade Rumors. Shortstop Carlos Correa holds a massive deal worth $60.5 million through 2028, with the Twins still owing $30 million as part of a trade. First baseman Christian Walker is locked in for $20 million through 2027. Pitcher Josh Hader costs $38 million through 2028. These big contracts limit the team’s ability to sign new talent. They must manage these dollars carefully to stay competitive. Several key players face decisions soon. Tatsuya Imai declined an opt-out after 2026, so he stays for two more years and $36 million. However, he can opt out after 2027. The team also exercised a $13.35 million option on infielder Isaac Paredes. But they declined a $5 million option on pitcher Ryan Weiss, choosing a $500 thousand buyout instead. This mix of options shows a team trying to balance cost and talent. They cannot afford to be too rigid with their money. The Core Fades While Others Rise The trend lines for Houston are moving down. Former stars like Alex Bregman, Justin Verlander, Framber Valdez, and Kyle Tucker are long gone. After capturing 106 wins and a title in 2022, the club posted 90, 88, 87, and 81 victories over the last four seasons. They missed the playoffs entirely in 2025. The 2026 season was a fluke. No other team had previously made the postseason in a complete season with a losing record until they did. That record does not look good on a resume. Free agents like LaMonte Wade Jr., Jake Meyers, and Daulton Varsho will leave soon. The team needs to fill these holes without breaking the bank. The farm system has suffered from penalties related to the sign-stealing scandal. This makes the upcoming years critical for the franchise. If they do not find new talent soon, the window will close completely. The Astros must act fast to rebuild their core before it is too late.

item.title: John Harbaugh Turned The Giants Into NFC East Favorites
item.description: Thomas Shea-Imagn Images The New York Giants sit in first place in the NFC East, and the shift started with a new coach who refuses to let mistakes slide. John Harbaugh has turned this team around in his first season by demanding total accountability from every player on the roster. Yahoo Sports reports the Giants (4-2-1) are the only team in the division with a winning record as they head into their next matchup. This success comes after the team matched its win total from last year before the season even reached the midway point. Harbaugh did not wait for a crisis to fix the culture. He met with player groups in the locker room immediately after a loss in Los Angeles to stop any self-pity from taking hold. That quick action helped the team bounce back from losing quarterback Jaxson Dart for the season the next morning. Calling Out Traitors to Fix Effort The biggest change is how the staff handles bad effort. Defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson addressed his unit’s lack of hustle in front of the entire team after a loss to New Orleans. He did not whisper to individuals or hold a side meeting. “You confront it. Just like we do, we confront everything,” Wilson said. He told players he looks at those who do not run to the ball as traitors to the defense. Wilson made it clear that the team will either make adjustments to get those players off the field or wait for them to correct their behavior. Harbaugh and his staff have removed players from the lineup when needed., including Jameis Winston and running back Cam Skattebo. Salary and veteran status mean nothing if the player cannot help the team win. Quarterback Moves That Win Games To secure the strongest opportunity against the Houston Texans, Harbaugh detailed last week’s decision to replace Winston with J.J. McCarthy. Many players found out about the change only when they started reviewing the game plan. There was no grand announcement. The move was met with such nonchalance by Harbaugh that he allowed the facts to speak for themselves. Although Jameis Winston had recorded two wins and a tie across his four starts, the staff determined a change was necessary for that specific week. Harbaugh said of his tactics, “I don’t know if it’s philosophy so much.” He added, “It’s just a week-to-week feel thing with your guys.” The Giants now face the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday, Nov. 8, at 1 p.m. ET at Lincoln Financial Field. The Eagles hold a 2-6 record, but the Giants have not won there since 2013. Harbaugh’s team has been on the field for a final play in five straight games and has lost just once in those tight spots.

item.description: Bremerton High School basketball star Jalen Davis is close to choosing his college destination. item.title: Toronto FC’s Comeback Streak Finally Snaps In Atlanta
item.description: Jordan Godfree-Imagn Images The magic ran out on Sunday night in Atlanta. For months, Toronto FC found a way to claw back into games, but that resilience hit a hard wall at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. The 3-1 loss officially ended the team’s season and their playoff hopes for the sixth straight year. This was not a game they could lose, yet they gave up two early goals that broke their spirit before halftime. Miguel Almiron opened the scoring for the hosts in the 22nd minute. Toronto could not mount a comeback this time. Coach Robin Fraser told reporters that the early mistakes were “soft goals” that changed the entire game. He stated that conceding two goals at the start rendered the remainder of the match desperate. “We’ve been talking about moments all year, and we end up giving up a couple of soft goals, and that changed everything,” Fraser said to reporters, according to Waking The Red . The team simply ran out of time to fix the mess. The Injury Toll and the Hole They Dug Fraser pointed to the first half of the season as a major reason for the struggle. “I do think that the injuries in the first half of the season really hurt us,” Fraser said, according to Yahoo Sports . Those missed players left gaps that Atlanta exploited with ease. A total of 63 goals conceded by Toronto this year, 19 higher than the 2025 figure, reveals the extent of the damage. Finishing 12th with a 9-12-12 record, they reached the final weekend. With no path to close the gap, they remained four points behind the playoff threshold. Even though Lewis Morgan scored a late goal in the 79th minute, it was too little, too late. That was the only shot on target to score for the visitors. Captain Jonathan Osorio knew the group had the talent to make it but fell short. “I’m just very disappointed that we weren’t able to make the playoffs this year with the team that we have,” Osorio said. The fans watched their team fight hard all year, but the defense could not hold the line when it mattered most. History Repeats Itself in Georgia Mercedes-Benz Stadium remains a house of horrors for this squad. Atlanta has not seen a Toronto victory since the 2019 MLS Eastern Conference final match. The pattern of late collapses finally broke, but not in their favor. Comebacks after the 80th minute generated 18 points this season, accounting for almost half their overall tally. You cannot live on hope forever, and this loss proves it. According to reports, the decisive factor was allowing two goals before halftime. The season ends with a trip to Philadelphia on Saturday, November 7. The team faces the Union on MLS Decision Day, but the playoff race is already over for them. “We had some moments that let us down, and when you go down, give up a goal, it changes the game,” Fraser added. The reality is clear. For the sixth consecutive season, Toronto FC will be absent from the postseason. The comeback streak is dead, and the rebuilding starts now.

item.title: Lions' Jack Campbell releases statement on progress of neck injury
item.description: Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell has full movement in his lower body and is continuing to make progress with movement in his upper body, according to a statement he released through the team on Wednesday, Nov. 4. Campbell is continuing to make progress following a serious neck injury that forced him to be carted off the field and immediately hospitalized in a 19-15 win over the Minnesota Vikings . "My family and I want to sincerely thank everyone for the overwhelming amount of love, prayers, and support we’ve received over the past few days. It means more to us than words can express," the statement said. "I’m incredibly encouraged by the progress I’ve made in such a short period of time. I have full movement in my lower body, and I’m continuing to make progress with movement in my upper body. I know there’s still work ahead, but I remain very optimistic. I’m taking things one day at a time, staying positive, and focusing on getting better." On the opening play of the fourth quarter in Sunday's win, Campbell went limp on what appeared to be a routine tackle of tight end T.J. Hockenson and received on-field medical attention for several minutes before being carted off on a stretcher and taken immediately to a local hospital. "My faith in God has never been stronger," Campbell's statement continued. "I know He has a plan for me, and I trust in that plan. I know there may be challenges ahead, but with my faith, my family, and so many people in my corner, I know we’ll get through this. "I especially want to thank the athletic trainers and medical personnel who responded and cared for me on the field. I know those were difficult moments, and I’m incredibly grateful for the professionalism, compassion, and care you showed me. The way you handled everything and looked after me when I needed it most is something I’ll never forget. From the bottom of my heart, thank you. "I also can’t say enough about the incredible care I’ve received from the medical team at Henry Ford Hospital and the Detroit Lions medical staff. They’ve been amazing to me and my family throughout this process, and I’m truly grateful for everything they’ve done. "To my teammates, coaches, and everyone in the Lions organization, I want you to know how much I love and appreciate you. This team is a family to me, and the way everyone has been there for me means everything. I’m proud to be a Detroit Lion and couldn’t ask to be surrounded by a better group of people. "One thing I’ve learned about Detroit is that this city is built on toughness, resilience, and grit. That’s exactly how I’m going to approach this challenge. "Please continue to keep me and my family in your prayers. We feel the love, and I can’t thank everyone enough. "God is good. My faith is strong." The statement is the first we've heard from Campbell since the injury. The Lions released a statement at 7:08 p.m. on Sunday that Campbell was resting and would remain at the hospital for continued evaluation and monitoring
